title: Onboarding saga background thread never transitions onboarding_registry row from 'pending' to terminal state (completed/failed)
description: POST /api/v1/onboarding inserts a 'pending' row into tenant_default.onboarding_registry and returns 201. A detached background thread (runSagaBackground in src/api/routes/onboarding.zig, spawned via std.Thread.spawn + thread.detach()) is expected to call onboarding_mod.executeSaga and then persistOnboardingResult to update the row to 'completed' or 'failed'. The update never happens — 20/20 rows observed during the WF03-onboarding-e2e-fix-20260614 Step 04 test run remain state='pending', response_status=201, completed_at=NULL indefinitely. This blocks onb-ui-03 (saga terminal), onb-ui-04 (completed result + page-reload restore), the onboarding pipeline test, and the real onboarding user journey. Keycloak (localhost:8081) and DB (localhost:5433) were both healthy during the test run.
root_cause: Threadlocal tenant context isolation: the request thread sets tenant_context._current (threadlocal) to the platform admin tenant, causing pool.acquire() to apply search_path=tenant_default on connections. The background saga thread (runSagaBackground) runs in a DIFFERENT thread and has the DEFAULT threadlocal state (no tenant set). When persistOnboardingResult acquires a pool connection from the background thread, that connection gets search_path=public (or no tenant schema). The UPDATE onboarding_registry WHERE onboarding_id=... therefore hits public.onboarding_registry (always empty) rather than tenant_default.onboarding_registry (where the row was inserted by the request thread). 0 rows are matched, the state never transitions, and the catch {} swallows the no-op silently. UPDATE 2026-08-09 (discovered during WF03-GH352-20260809 / ISS-0097 investigation): the fix applied for this issue (persistOnboardingResult in src/api/routes/onboarding.zig, ~line 537) hardcodes 'UPDATE tenant_default.onboarding_registry ...'. migrations/056_onboarding_registry.sql declares '-- scope: public' and creates the table only in public; a tenant_default copy existed for a time as an unintended dual-schema shadow (see docs/anti-patterns.md), which is why the tenant_default-qualified UPDATE worked when this fix was written. migrations/GBL-134_iss0185_drop_global_registry_shadows.sql (ISS-0185, GH #518) subsequently dropped onboarding_registry from tenant_default as one of the shadow tables it correctly cleaned up, but persistOnboardingResult's hardcoded qualifier was never updated to match. Confirmed live against this workspace's bpm_test on 2026-08-09T17:27Z: a direct 'UPDATE tenant_default.onboarding_registry ...' throws 'ERROR: relation "tenant_default.onboarding_registry" does not exist'; pg_class/pg_namespace confirms onboarding_registry now exists only in public. Every background-thread saga completion (success or failure path) now fails to persist its terminal state via this NEW mechanism, reproducing this issue's original symptom (rows stuck at state='pending' forever). This was never verified fixed in the first place: GH-285's own 2026-07-29 triage note reads 'LIKELY_FIXED ... Confirm with a test run, then set RESOLVED' and that confirmation never happened before GBL-134 invalidated the fix anyway. The correct qualifier is 'public.onboarding_registry', not 'tenant_default.onboarding_registry'.
affected_areas: migrations/GBL-134_iss0185_drop_global_registry_shadows.sql (dropped the tenant_default shadow copy persistOnboardingResult's fix had come to depend on)
error_detail: All 20 rows in tenant_default.onboarding_registry stuck at state='pending', response_status=201, completed_at=NULL. The detached background thread never updates the row, indicating a silent panic, deadlock, or early return inside runSagaBackground / executeSaga before persistOnboardingResult is reached.
resolution: Fixed during WF03-GH652-20260810 (ISS-0647 triage) while root-causing a different but adjacent test failure (onboarding_realm_guard_test.zig TC-ISS0071-01, in markOnboardingRealmMissing() in the same file). That investigation independently rediscovered this exact regression -- persistOnboardingResult() (src/api/routes/onboarding.zig, ~line 537 at time of fix) still hardcoded 'UPDATE tenant_default.onboarding_registry ...', which throws C42P01 'relation does not exist' since onboarding_registry has only ever lived in public (confirmed via migrations/056_onboarding_registry.sql and every later migration touching it) and GBL-134 dropped the tenant_default shadow copy this call site had come to depend on, exactly as this issue's root_cause field already documented. Fixed by correcting the qualifier to 'public.onboarding_registry' in both persistOnboardingResult() and the sibling function markOnboardingRealmMissing() (which had the identical bug, also fixed in the same pass).
prevention: Both call sites now carry inline comments citing this issue and explaining why 'public' (not 'tenant_default') is correct, with a pointer to the migration history. No new lint rule added -- this specific class (schema-qualified literal referencing a table that has since moved) is the same one lint_test_isolation.py / lint_sql_param_types.py do not currently check for hardcoded production-code schema qualifiers (only test fixtures and $N parameter casts respectively); a future enhancement could add a check that greps for `<schema>.<table>` literals in src/ and cross-references them against the schema each table's CREATE TABLE migration actually used.

related_issues.relation: prior partial match — same symptom (saga stuck pending) was worked around by rewriting tests to avoid createTestTenant; underlying backend defect was never fixed

GBL-134 (ISS-0185 global-registry shadow-table cleanup, GH #518) dropped tenant_default.onboarding_registry, which persistOnboardingResult had been relying on since this issue's original fix. The cleanup itself was correct per ISS-0185's goal; this call site's hardcoded schema qualifier was never updated to match.

discovered incidentally while investigating ISS-0097 (GH-352)'s requested production-impact grep for std.Thread.spawn call sites that touch pool.acquire(). Same architectural root (threadlocal tenant_context does not propagate across a std.Thread.spawn boundary), different concrete symptom and fix.
